title: Spanning Tree on Junos: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A department store adds a second emergency exit. Extra paths in a network can cause loops. Spanning tree keeps them safe.

lines.t: S T P keeps them safe

scenes.heading: The escape routes
scenes.narration: Shoppers can use any exit, but if every exit stays open, a crowd can circle forever. So some exits stay closed until they're needed. One switch is chosen as the boss. Backup exits stay closed. The old way is slow to reopen. The new way is quick.

scenes.heading: STP vs RSTP
scenes.narration: The two differ in speed and states. Classic S T P has five port states. R S T P has three, and recovers in seconds. And on Juniper E X switches, R S T P is the default. STP has five states, and RSTP has three. RSTP recovers in just a second or two. And it's the default on E X switches.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three misconceptions. They're different standards, not a rebrand. In a stable network, some ports stay blocked. And the root is chosen by priority and M A C, not location.

items.wrong: STP and RSTP are the same
The root is the most central switch
items.right: It's the lowest priority, then lowest MAC

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos STP lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Spanning tree blocks extra paths to stop loops. R S T P is faster, with three states. Check it with show spanning tree. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos STP lab.
